title: Async Python Practice Exam
description: Practice async def, await, and asyncio.run for concurrent I/O-style workflows.

questions.prompt: async def defines a coroutine function that can be awaited.
questions.explanation: Coroutines cooperate with an event loop instead of blocking on I/O.

questions.prompt: await pauses an async function until:
questions.explanation: await yields control so other tasks can run.

questions.prompt: asyncio.run(main()) is used to:
options: Run the top-level async main() from sync code
questions.explanation: run creates an event loop, runs main(), and closes it.

questions.prompt: Blocking time.sleep() inside async code can hurt concurrency.
questions.explanation: Prefer await asyncio.sleep() for async-friendly delays.

questions.prompt: asyncio.create_task(coro) schedules:
options: A coroutine to run concurrently on the loop
questions.explanation: Tasks let multiple coroutines progress together.

questions.prompt: await asyncio.gather(a(), b()) runs:
options: Multiple awaitables and waits for all
questions.explanation: gather is common for parallel async work.

questions.prompt: Async helps most when work is:
options: I/O bound (waiting on network, disk, sleep)
CPU bound math on one core always
questions.explanation: CPU-heavy work may need multiprocessing instead.

questions.prompt: Calling an async function without await returns a coroutine object.
questions.explanation: You must await it or schedule it on a loop.

questions.prompt: async with supports:
options: Async context managers that need await on enter/exit
questions.explanation: Some resources expose async __aenter__/__aexit__.

questions.prompt: The event loop:
questions.explanation: asyncio drives coroutine execution.

questions.prompt: await asyncio.sleep(1) during async code:
options: Yields for about one second without blocking the whole thread like time.sleep
questions.explanation: Other tasks can run during the sleep.

questions.prompt: async/await is built into Python syntax and the asyncio library.
questions.explanation: Third-party libs add async APIs on top of the same model.

questions.prompt: A common bug is forgetting await, which leads to:
options: Coroutines that never ran and 'coroutine was never awaited' warnings
questions.explanation: Always await coroutines you intend to run.

questions.prompt: Concurrent vs parallel in beginner terms:
options: Concurrent tasks take turns; parallel may use multiple CPUs
questions.explanation: Async concurrency is often single-threaded cooperation.

questions.prompt: import asyncio is needed for:
options: run, sleep, gather, and other loop utilities
questions.explanation: asyncio is the standard library async framework.

questions.prompt: You can mix sync and async code but boundaries need care (await from async only).
questions.explanation: Do not call blocking sync I/O heavily inside async functions.

questions.prompt: async for is used to:
questions.explanation: Async generators produce items with await between steps.

questions.prompt: When learning async, start with:
options: Small scripts using asyncio.run and one or two coroutines
questions.explanation: Build mental model before large apps.

questions.prompt: Task cancellation in asyncio requires:
questions.explanation: Advanced topic; be aware cleanup may be needed.

questions.prompt: Not every program needs async; use it when I/O waiting is the bottleneck.
questions.explanation: Simple scripts are fine with synchronous code.
